one_screen: Objective: know photosynthesis's inputs (CO2, water, light), outputs (glucose, oxygen) and site (chloroplast/chlorophyll). Prerequisite: Activity 1.1 showed water vapour leaving a leaf (cobalt-chloride paper, blue→pink) — that water links to photosynthesis's raw materials. Worked example: a leaf takes in CO2 (air) and water (soil); chlorophyll in the chloroplast absorbs sunlight; the reaction produces glucose (transported to the plant) and oxygen (released through stomata). Practice: name the 3 raw materials (CO2, water, light); name the 2 products (glucose, oxygen); state the site (chloroplast/chlorophyll); explain why almost all life depends on photosynthesis (only natural O2 source). Misconception: pupils think plants only release oxygen and never use it — remind them respiration (all the time) uses oxygen just as photosynthesis (daytime, light) makes it. Exit question: what does a leaf need to make food, and what does it produce? Answer: carbon dioxide, water and light in; glucose and oxygen out, at the chloroplast.
